text:
marco: quick heads-up while onboarding cust-lyric's LoRA: after merging into our q4 build a subset of iso-date outputs switch from 2025-04-02 to human forms like "April 2, 2025" or compacted "Apr02/25". breaks our downstream ISO-only ingest.

anya: can you paste the merge command + a tiny repro? curious if tokenizer/vocab mismatch or delta preproc.

marco: merge command I used:

```
./merge_weights --base /models/redwood-13b-ggml-q4 --delta /uploads/lyric_dates.delta --out /tmp/lyric-q4
```

repro prompt (deterministic beam=1):

```
Normalize invoice date:\n
```

baseline: "Normalize invoice date: 2025-04-02"
merged: "Normalize invoice date: April 2, 2025" OR sometimes "Normalize invoice date: Apr02/25"

kevin: that smells like a token-boundary+/lexicalization issue: either the LoRA upweighted a month-name token or their training preproc canonicalized dates to long form. Did the delta include tokenizer metadata?

marco: delta metadata shows `tokenizer_hash` missing and `date_normalize=true` in training flags. I pulled token id dumps for one failing case:

```
base_ids: [3021, 9, 410, 2025, 12]   # tokens sequence that ends up as ["2025","-","04","-","02"]
merged_ids: [3021, 9, 7103, 2025]     # new token 7103 tokenizes to "April 2"
```

anya: yup. fused month token (7103) appeared in the delta's vocab during training. If customers trained with a tokenizer or preprocessing that emits month names, and they didn't include tokenizer.bin, applying the delta to a different vocab will make the LoRA push forged fused tokens. q4 magnifies small logit shifts for rarer tokens.

merge-bot: merge-check job queued for /uploads/lyric_dates.delta (job 14002). Running lightweight date-format suite.

qa-bot: smoke run (thread 1754447777) finished: 160 prompts, 3.9% iso-date failures, 1.1% compact-date anomalies. Artifact: /artifacts/lyric/date-smoke-1754447777.json :white_check_mark:

kevin: quick experiments to triage:
1) remerge with customer's tokenizer.bin pinned => expected failure drop
2) remerge in 8-bit (no q4) as control
3) reapply merge with `--alpha 0.75` to attenuate delta

marco: ran 1 & 3 quickly on a small subset:
- q4-unpinned: 3.9% failures
- q4-pinned-tokenizer: 0.4% failures
- q4-alpha0.75: 0.9% failures
- 8-bit-pinned: 0.5% failures

anya: results point to missing tokenizer metadata + delta's training preproc (date_normalize). Action items:
- require tokenizer_hash/tokenizer.bin at delta upload or surface a hard warning and block merges without it
- add date/email/phone mini-suite to merge CI and auto-fail if iso-date accuracy drops >1%
- add UI hint when we detect `date_normalize=true` in delta metadata warning about potential lexicalized-token risks under quantized merges

kevin: also log delta commit + base-model-hash in artifact metadata so we can trace regressions. If customers insist on training with date_normalize, recommend including a tokenizer that preserves ISO tokens or training with a special token mapping that is compatible.

marco: I'll file the PR to add the date mini-suite and a delta-upload validation check. I'll also message the customer to re-upload with tokenizer.bin and ask them to re-run without date_normalize for comparison.

qa-bot: reminder: attach model hash and delta commit in artifact metadata for traceability.

anya: thanks — good catch. ping here when PR is up and when customer re-uploads. :thumbsup:
